title: Triangle of Sadness - Equality and Ideologies

commenti.body: Why would a Swedish director make a movie about American politics? I think you're interpreting the movie a little too much through an American lens. I think the movie is broadly about power, and how power changes people, and those concepts don't only apply to America.

You don't have a thesis here, you're just flailing around to various surface-level facts and failing to see past your own politics. 

I think it's trying to illustrate that the true engine of human suffering is hierarchy itself. The Capitalist/Communist divide can easily be one of self-interest and circumstantial convenience, or worse still just set dressing for authoritarian oppression. If you don't solve the problem of unjust hierarchy, then you haven't really solved anything, only changed the people on top of the hierarchy.

I recently grabbed this movie from my local library, knowing nothing about it.  

I think there's an obvious open for political commentary/discourse.  So if that's your interest, you can find it in the movie.  

For me personally, it was just a wonderful film about power relations, and how people adapt to situations.  

Abigail only has power because the group becomes stranded and she knows how to fish.  Before that, she is of no use or interest because they're all on a ship where chefs are preparing all manner of food.  So, it's only appropriate that she comes to the foreground of the movie after the wreck.  And this is why she murders the other when the way out is found.  She had no position of power prior to the wreck, nor would she after.

It's one of the better movies I've seen as of late.  It jumps around and does unexpected things.  Choosing a modern cruise line as a setting paired with what could go wrong was just brilliant. And lots of brilliant little moments sprinkled between.  

But yeah I could feel that during the scenes where the ships life was in question, there was a political edge, and it permeates throughout the film.  But it's good because it doesn't rely on these ideas.  It's very much open to interpretation.  And the focus is on the people and their positions of power.  

I think it's one of the better modern movies.  It shows people existing in this time period very much in the way they exist.  A disastrous relationship based on Instagram photos. It captures the modern world well.  Even the captain no longer exists...he's just drunken and ready to sink. He's overcome by ideas.  He took a job as captain of a ship that basically steers itself.  (One scene shows quests inquiring about sails they thought they saw...leading towards the captains ultimate self-imposed doom.)

It's a unique movie.  It was probably better because I watched it without knowing anything about it.  But I could watch it again.
